learn.intro: One email can show many warning signs. Instead of asking Jev ten separate times, ask all ten yes or no questions in a single request. Each sign comes back with its own probability, so you can see which ones lit up and how sure Jev is.

compare.title: Jev, ten Nouls in one request
points: One call carries all ten questions
Each answer is its own probability

compare.title: An LLM, asked for ten answers
points: Returns ten true or false fields
Pays for every token it writes
No probability to tell sure from unsure

why: A single request can carry many questions. Jev answers them together, so asking for ten signs costs little more than asking for one.
Each sign has a probability, so a sign at 53 percent reads very differently from one at 97 percent. That is the cue to send a borderline email to a person.
Both racers are scored on each sign, so a racer that gets 9 of 10 signs right on an email earns most of the credit for it.

questions.prompt: What is the benefit of putting many Nouls in one request?

options.text: Many answers for one fast, cheap call
Jev can then write an explanation

questions.explanation: Jev answers them together, so extra questions add little time or cost. It does not make answers perfect, and Jev still returns typed answers only.

questions.prompt: Why does each sign come with a probability?

options.text: It shows how sure Jev is, so unsure ones can be reviewed
It sets the price of the call

questions.explanation: A probability near 50 percent flags a borderline call worth a second look.
